title: However, Nevertheless: Contrast in Santa Cruz

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know *sin embargo* and *aunque* from A2 Unit 28, and *no obstante* from B1 Unit 1. They set one idea against another: good news against a problem, or a fact against a doubt. Santa Cruz is a region full of such contrasts: fast growth and large fields on one side, forest loss and fires on the other. *Sin embargo* and *no obstante* start a new clause and are followed by a comma.

sections.title: Connectors of contrast
rows: Santa Cruz es una ciudad muy grande; sin embargo, hace unas décadas era mucho más pequeña.
Santa Cruz is a very large city; however, a few decades ago it was much smaller.
La soya es un producto importante. No obstante, necesita mucha tierra.
Soya is an important product. Nevertheless, it needs a lot of land.
Aunque hay mucho ganado, la región también produce soya y caña de azúcar.
Although there is a lot of cattle, the region also produces soya and sugar cane.
A pesar de los incendios, la región sigue creciendo.
In spite of the fires, the region keeps growing. (*a pesar de* + noun)

items.spanish: La agroindustria crea empleo; sin embargo, algunas personas critican el desmonte.
items.english: Agribusiness creates jobs; however, some people criticise the clearing of forest.

items.spanish: El campo produce mucho. No obstante, los incendios preocupan a los ambientalistas.
items.english: The countryside produces a lot. Nevertheless, the fires worry environmentalists.

items.spanish: Aunque Santa Cruz es una ciudad moderna, conserva sus fiestas tradicionales.
items.english: Although Santa Cruz is a modern city, it keeps its traditional festivals.

sections.content: Do not stop at one connector: choose it by the relation. *Sin embargo* and *no obstante* mark the second idea as a contrast (the formal one is *no obstante*). *Aunque* can start the sentence or sit in the middle: *Aunque hay incendios, la región crece* or *La región crece aunque hay incendios*.
